html:
The Central African Republic became independent from France on 13 August 1960, with David Dacko as its first president.

The country inherited little from colonial rule: few schools, almost no roads, and an economy of cotton, coffee and diamonds. Dacko, a relative of the dead founder Boganda, made it a one-party state.

On the last night of 1965 his army chief Bokassa seized power. Since then the country has had many coups and mutinies, French troops have intervened again and again, and the state has rarely controlled much beyond Bangui. It was part of the wave of the Year of Africa.
sum: The Central African Republic became independent from France on 13 August 1960, with David Dacko as its first president.
